label: prf:topological-mass
title: Proof of Topological Decomposition of Mass
html:
The proof proceeds in four steps: decomposition of the mass integral using the descent involution, identification of the descended term with the unknot-core holonomy, localisation of the transient terms to exceptional divisors, and evaluation via the symmetric q-dilogarithm.

By (eigenspace decomposition of the mass integrand), the descent involution \hat{\tau}_n produces an orthogonal Killing-form decomposition of the multiplicative integral. Orthogonality makes squared norms add, not norms; for the norms themselves the triangle inequality gives

  \mathfrak{m}(\varrho)
  \le
  \bigl\lVert \mathrm{MI}\!\!\int_\Sigma \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha) \bigr\rVert +
  \bigl\lVert \mathrm{MI}\!\!\int_\Sigma (\alpha - \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha)) \bigr\rVert.

By (descended term is the unknot-core holonomy), the first summand equals \lVert \mathrm{Hol}_{\nabla_A}(\varrho_0; \mathfrak{G}) \rVert. By (transient terms are bounded by exceptional-divisor contributions), the second summand is at most \sum_{i=1}^{N} \lVert \mathrm{MI}\!\!\int_{E_i} (\nabla_A q, L \wedge F^+) \rVert. Combining these yields

  \mathfrak{m}(\varrho)
  \le
  \bigl\lVert \mathrm{Hol}_{\nabla_A}(\varrho_0; \mathfrak{G}) \bigr\rVert +
  \sum_{i=1}^{N}
  \bigl\lVert \mathrm{MI}\!\!\int_{E_i} (\nabla_A q, L \wedge F^+) \bigr\rVert,

the upper bound of 11.1.16 in its archimedean form, and an upper bound for the conjectured decomposition eq:topological-mass-decomp. Equality, and hence the conjectured decomposition itself, would need equality in both inequalities above. Both are open: neither is forced by the disc splitting and support hypotheses. If each exceptional-divisor summand equals the symmetric q-dilogarithm -\mathrm{Li}_2^q(-z_i), as the symmetric q-dilogarithm evaluation conjectures, then the bound reads \mathfrak{m}(\varrho) \le \lVert \mathrm{Hol}_{\nabla_A}(\varrho_0; \mathfrak{G}) \rVert + \sum_{i=1}^{N} \bigl(-\mathrm{Li}_2^q(-z_i)\bigr). \square
